newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, nearbys up with cash.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, nearbys up with cash.

text.p: A stronger tone to both boxed beef and fed cattle markets kept nearby CME live cattle futures strong at the close while deferreds were pressured by higher corn futures. Feeders ended mixed as strong cash sentiment offset early pressure from corn, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.725 cent higher to 0.175 lower with June up 0.375 at 64.575 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.150 to off 0.125 with May unchanged at 71.150 cents.
Active boxed beef sales this week and willingness by packers to raise bids for fed cattle pushed live cattle futures higher, traders said.
"It was the time period when we had expected by the middle of this week we would start to see a little firmness" in beef, said Bob VandeVorde with Farmers Marketing Resources.

"We will see 10 days or so of a nice firm tone in the boxed beef market and support (bullish) attitudes. Most of the people you talk to think we will see $68 cash cattle trade next week in Texas and Kansas," VandeVorde said.
Technicals also lent support. June looked technically firm after closing through a trendline Wednesday, chartists said.
Weather concerns from a storm moving across the Midwest also provided support, traders added.
R.J. O'Brien end LFG bought April late while Cargill Investor Services bought June. R.J. O'Brien sold June late but remained a net buyer, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought 70 calls and sold 66 calls. They also bought June 68 calls and August 66 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures recovered along with paring of losses in deferred live cattle and support generated by expectations of further gains in the CME feeder cattle index. Demand for feeders for both grazing and feedlot replacement remains strong, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.17 at $71.25 per cwt, the highest level since February 24, 1995.

"More of the demand is coming from the lighter weight cattle to put on grass, and with prices going up the lighter weight cattle is supporting the heavier weights," said Dale Benson, senior livestock analyst for Dean Witter.

Some traders cited continued concern that poor weather was affecting the calf crop, especially with reports of death loss in the Dakotas following a recent snowstorm and flooding. But analysts said the calf losses would affect back months more than nearbys.

Feeders had started lower on pressure from the higher corn futures and selling prompted by an apparent overbought condition. Much of Wednesday's gains came from short-covering and not new buying as had been expected, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services and E.D.&F. Man bought May while Refco sold late. Prudential Securities sold early, pit sources said.
